title: Shopping Center Lease (Triple Net): Alder Crossing Shopping Center, Suite C-7
fictional_notice: All parties and facts are invented.

defects.title: No CASp inspection statement
defects.why: The accessibility section allocates ADA and Title 24 compliance costs but the lease never states whether the premises have had a Certified Access Specialist inspection and has no statutory CASp notice paragraph.

defects.title: 20 percent recurring late charge stacked with default interest
defects.why: The late charge is 20 percent of the overdue amount for every month or part of a month, with no grace period, and it accrues together with default interest on the same amount. That is hard to square with a reasonable estimate of the landlord's cost of a late payment.
quotes: a late charge equal to twenty percent (20%) of the overdue amount for each month or part of a month that the amount remains unpaid
The late charge is in addition to interest under Section 4.4, and both shall accrue on the same overdue amount.

defects.title: Operating costs include amounts reimbursed by insurance or third parties
defects.why: The lease recites that the tenant is a qualified commercial tenant, yet repair costs are charged in full even when the landlord recovers them from insurance, a warranty or a third party, with no credit. Costs reimbursed by insurance or a third party cannot be included.
quotes: whether or not Landlord later recovers insurance proceeds, warranty payments or reimbursement from another tenant or third party on account of the same cost, and Landlord shall not be required to credit any such recovery against Operating Costs

defects.title: Operating cost share set in landlord's sole discretion
defects.why: The tenant's share of operating costs is whatever the landlord assigns in its sole discretion and need not be proportionate to floor area or follow any written method. For a qualified commercial tenant the costs must be allocated proportionately by square footage or another documented method.
quotes: in such manner as Landlord determines in its sole discretion, which need not be proportionate to the floor area of the Premises or follow any fixed or written method

defects.title: Security deposit returned 90 days after expiration
defects.why: The deposit is to be returned within 90 days after the Expiration Date. A commercial deposit must be returned no later than 30 days from the date the landlord receives possession.
quotes: to Tenant within ninety (90) days after the Expiration Date, together with a written statement of any amounts applied

defects.title: Section 1951.4 remedy with sole-discretion consent to transfers
defects.why: The lease invokes the continuation remedy of section 1951.4 but lets the landlord withhold consent to any assignment or sublease in its sole and absolute discretion. The remedy is available only if the tenant may sublet or assign subject at most to reasonable standards or consent not unreasonably withheld.
quotes: Landlord may grant or withhold its consent to any proposed Transfer in Landlord's sole and absolute discretion, for any reason or for no reason
may keep this Lease in effect and enforce all of its rights under this Lease, including the right to recover Rent as it becomes due

defects.title: Month-to-month rent increase of any amount on 10 days' notice
defects.why: During the consensual month-to-month holdover the landlord may raise rent by any amount on 10 days' notice. For a qualified commercial tenant on a month-to-month tenancy an increase needs at least 30 days' written notice, and 90 days if it is more than 10 percent.
quotes: Landlord may increase Monthly Base Rent by any amount, effective ten (10) days after written notice of the increase is delivered to Tenant
